LIVE PROOF, the incident's own precondition. At landing time two files staged by T863
(docs/infra/races/protocol-compliance.md, findings/T863-protocol-compliance-race.json) were
sitting in the shared index -- b47c248's setup exactly. 5d66dd1 contains exactly its five named
paths and BOTH of T863's files are still staged and uncommitted afterwards. Pre-fix the same

THE MECHANISM, ESTABLISHED BY REPRODUCTION AND NOT BY ARGUMENT. b47c248 (2026-08-24) carries
T891's four files -- bin/subagent, build.zig, tools/regression-lane-telemetry-parity.sh,
findings/T891-lane-telemetry-parity.json -- under T901's message. The wrapper's four guarantees
were all satisfied on the way in, and the T547 flock was held. The reproduction (arm 1, 3/3 runs
pre-fix) shows why: the lock serialises COMMITTERS, and only wrapper invocations take it. T891
staged with a bare `git add -- <paths>`, which takes no lock and needs none. Timeline:

  1. T901's wrapper acquires the mutex, `git add -f -- <its paths>`, snapshots the staged set,
     finds nothing foreign, elects COMMIT_MODE=index;
  2. T891's bare `git add -- <4 paths>` writes the SHARED .git/index inside that window;
  3. T901's plain `git commit` builds its tree from the whole index -> T891's four files land.

Verified with plain git that this is git's actual behaviour and that the alternative is not: an
index-mode `git commit` picks up the foreign paths, a pathspec `git commit -m msg -- <paths>`
does not and leaves them staged. So the capture path is precisely COMMIT_MODE=index, i.e. the
healthy path, taken whenever the staged-set snapshot was clean when it was read.

  The general fact worth keeping: SERIALISING ACCESS TO SHARED MUTABLE STATE IS NOT THE SAME AS
  NOT SHARING IT. The mutex was correct and insufficient. Any guard that reads shared state and
  then acts on it has a window; the only closure is for the state not to be shared.

THE FIX, AND THE ONE THAT WAS NOT CHOSEN. Private index (GIT_INDEX_FILE), seeded from HEAD by
`git read-tree HEAD` (or --empty on an unborn HEAD), held for the whole stage->verify->commit
span, exported so `git commit` and its hooks resolve it. Another console's staging is then not
merely refused but INVISIBLE -- structurally incapable of entering this commit. Three properties
came free and are each covered by an arm:

  (a) a refused invocation no longer deposits its own staging in shared state. Pre-fix the
      wrapper staged THEN verified THEN refused, leaving its paths in .git/index for the next
      committer to absorb -- measured in the live-clone baseline smoke, where both refused
      consoles left `A docs/status/CURRENT.md` and `M docs/status/HANDOVER.md` staged. The guard
      against sweeping was itself seeding sweeps.
  (b) foreign staged content no longer BLOCKS a correct commit. Pre-fix, a path another console
      staged and this row never touched refused this row's commit ("index contains staged paths
      outside your scope"). In the live-clone baseline that cost 6 of 6 commits across 3 runs.
      Capture and blockage are one defect, and only the second one was visible as an error.
  (c) the pre-commit backstop stops judging the wrong index (see the hook finding below).

REJECTED: the pathspec commit form (`git commit -m msg -- <paths>`), which the bundle names as the
alternative. It does prevent capture -- verified directly -- and it is fewer moving parts. What it
would have cost: staging still goes through the SHARED index, so (a) and (b) both survive
unfixed; this row's `git add -f` keeps polluting shared state for every other console; and the
wrapper's "verify the staged set" guarantee degrades into a check on state it does not own. The
private index fixes the sharing; the pathspec form only fixes the symptom at the commit site. It
is also the weaker composition with the hook: git already sets GIT_INDEX_FILE to a temporary
index for a pathspec commit, so the hook had to learn to read it either way.

TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT NEEDED HANDLING, BOTH WITH THEIR OWN CONTROL.

1. SHARED-INDEX RECONCILE (arm 4). A commit built from a private index leaves the shared index
   holding each named path at its PRE-commit blob, so `git status` reads the file as staged for
   reversion and the next plain `git commit` by anyone would revert it. An isolation fix that
   manufactures a second sweep hazard is not a fix. The wrapper now `git reset -q --` its named
   paths in the shared index after the commit, while still holding the mutex (so two wrappers
   never contend for .git/index.lock). Paths another console had ALREADY staged before we started
   are skipped by name -- that entry is their staging, not our stale one, and unstaging it is the
   exact rule this wrapper exists to enforce. Arm 4 asserts `git diff --cached` and
   `git status --porcelain -uno` are both empty after a lone commit; it fails loudly if the
   reconcile is ever dropped.

2. BOTH HOOK GATES WERE JUDGING THE WRONG INDEX (arm 3 covers gate 2). tools/hooks/pre-commit unsets GIT_INDEX_FILE as
   part of the T771 git-env isolation. For this hook that variable is LOAD-BEARING: git points it
   at the index the commit is actually being built from. Unset, gate 2 read the SHARED .git/index
   instead, so a foreign path staged by another console read as a scope violation by THIS commit
   -- refusing a correct commit over content that could not enter it. This was already live for
   every pathspec (`--explicit`) commit and would have made the private index unusable. Fixed by
   saving the value before the unset and using it for the two reads that need it; everything
   the hook RUNS still runs with the git env cleared, so T771's guarantee is untouched.

   Gate 1 had the identical defect, found by it BLOCKING this row's own landing:
   `pre-commit: C2 regressed: 1 > floor 0`, where the one hit was
   `C10-NEW VOLATILE untracked/T863-protocol-compliance-race.md (at
   docs/infra/races/protocol-compliance.md)` -- T863's staged file, not mine. claimlint spawns
   its own `git diff --cached` (src/claimlint.zig:1346) to decide which evidence citations are
   NEW for the C10 ratchet, and with GIT_INDEX_FILE unset it read the shared index. So another
   console's staged content could fail THIS commit for a citation this commit does not contain.
   Fixed the same way, through a wz_claimlint wrapper so only claimlint gets the variable: gate 3
   runs regression scripts that `git init` scratch repos, and a stray GIT_INDEX_FILE would point
   their git at this commit's index (T849's incident class). After the fix the same commit read
   `claimlint ... C2=0 ... <= floor, allowed`.
   This one was not predicted; it was found because the fix's own landing tripped it. Gate 2's
   defect had an arm written for it; gate 1's did not, and the honest reason is that arm 3 only
   exercises the gate the bundle pointed at.

THE GUARD THAT BLINDED THE TESTS -- the reason this incident class had no failing control.
tools/git-commit-mine's T771 worktree guard refuses when HEAD holds fewer than 2000 files. Keyed
on tree SIZE alone it fired in every SCRATCH repo too, because a fixture repo legitimately holds
one file. Measured: before this change, regression-commit-concurrency.sh failed 6 of 6 arms with
"REFUSED -- HEAD holds only 1 files", and the same refusal was hitting
regression-git-commit-mine.sh, regression-git-commit-mine-hook.sh, regression-claim-lifecycle.sh
and regression-precommit.sh. The wrapper's entire mechanical test surface went dark the day the
guard landed, which is why the b47c248 sweep had nothing to catch it -- INCLUDING the T547 arm
whose stated purpose is "two concurrent runs, each commit contains ONLY its own paths". A guard
that silences the tests for its own subject matter costs more than it collects.
Fixed by gating invariant 2 on repository IDENTITY -- weizigo's root commit
ef58d0f45fd453fc850b9638d5527354c40f9f6f -- instead of on tree size. A truncated live repo still
has that root (truncation is a commit on top of it), so the guard keeps every bit of its coverage;
a `git init` fixture has a different root and is exempt. Invariant 1 (core.worktree) stays
unconditional. regression-commit-concurrency.sh went 0/6 -> 6/6 arms on this change alone, with
no edit to that file.

Gate 3 (fast test tier) is bypassed in the clone with the documented TEST_GATE_BYPASS escape and a
stated reason: a clone has no build artifacts, so regression-status-doc-truth.sh and smoke.sh fail
on "no managent binary". Gate 1 (claimlint) is stubbed clean for the same reason -- the clone has

and the smoke both exercise.

AN ENV LEAK OUT OF THE WRAPPER, found the same way. Gate 3 (fast test tier) selected
regression-git-commit-mine-hook.sh for this commit and it FAILED, having passed standalone and in
the sweep minutes earlier. Cause: tools/git-commit-mine exports GIT_MINE_EXPLICIT=1 for an
--explicit commit; `git commit` passes it to the hook; the hook passes it to gate 3's children;
and that script VARIES GIT_MINE_EXPLICIT per arm, reading it back with ${VAR:-0}. 6 of its 7 arms
silently ran the explicit branch instead of the branch they had set up -- reproduced directly with
`GIT_MINE_EXPLICIT=1 sh tools/regression-git-commit-mine-hook.sh` -> 6 FAILs. So every --explicit
commit in this repository that selected that script has been failing gate 3 for a reason with
nothing to do with the code under test. Fixed by unsetting the variables the script varies (plus
the git env, T849) at its top -- the same hygiene tools/regression-commit-isolation.sh ships with.
A check whose verdict depends on its caller's environment is not a check.

WHAT IS NOT FIXED, STATED PLAINLY.
  - A bare `git add` from any console still writes the shared index. Nothing here can stop that;
    what changed is that no wrapper commit can any longer see or capture it. The shared index
    remains a hazard for anyone who commits with plain `git commit`, where the pre-commit hook is
    the only backstop.
  - A directory pathspec (`tools/git-commit-mine docs/evidence -m ...`) still stages every changed
    file beneath it into the private index. The private index does not help there; the scope check
    does, and only in non---explicit mode. Not in scope for this row; worth a row of its own.
  - b47c248's attribution was NOT repaired. The bundle refused history rewriting on a shared fleet
    as dangerous; the incident is recorded instead, here and in
    findings/T891-lane-telemetry-parity.json (ccd3de8).
  - claimlint's `git diff --cached` (src/claimlint.zig) still reads whatever index its
    environment names. The hook now names the right one, but a direct `bin/weizigo-claimlint`
    run, and any other caller, still measures the shared index. src/claimlint.zig is held by
    another row; the reader-side fix belongs there, not here.
  - regression-precommit.sh's null control was already failing before this change and still fails:
    it runs the real hook against the live tree with MANAGENT_TASK_ID set, and T863 has two files
    staged in the shared index right now. Verified identical with the pre-change hook. It is one
    of the two scripts SWEEP-CONTRACT.md excludes from the superset comparison for exactly this
    reason ("The check's verdict is a function of what other consoles have uncommitted"). Those
    two staged T863 paths are, incidentally, a live instance of the b47c248 precondition.
